breakfast.name: Matapa
instructions: Pound cassava leaves
Cook with coconut milk, peanuts, garlic
Add shrimp
Simmer until thick
Serve with rice
breakfast.description: Cassava leaves in coconut-peanut sauce — Mozambique's signature dish.

breakfast.name: Pão com Manteiga (Bread and Butter)
instructions: Warm bread
Spread with butter
Serve with coffee

breakfast.name: Mapão (Bread Rolls)
instructions: The Portuguese brought wheat bread culture to Mozambique — colonized 1498-1975
Mapão are Mozambique's soft bread rolls — the Portuguese pão adapted
Mix flour, yeast, water, salt, oil into a smooth dough
Rise 1 hour
Shape into individual rolls
Rise again 30 minutes
Bake at 200°C until golden
The soft interior, slightly crusty exterior is the mapão texture
Eaten with butter, margarine, or used for sandwiches
Found at every padaria (bakery) across Mozambique's cities
The Portuguese bread tradition has become completely Mozambican
The padaria is the morning meeting place in Maputo and other cities
breakfast.description: Mozambique's Portuguese-legacy bread roll — soft wheat rolls baked golden, eaten at the padaria (bakery) that the Portuguese colonial presence (1498-1975) established. Mozambique's morning bread culture (padarias, coffee, rolls with butter) is a Portuguese legacy that has become completely local. The padaria is the morning gathering place in Maputo.

breakfast.name: Manhã de Manga (Mango Morning)
instructions: Mozambique grows some of the finest mangoes in the world — the climate and soil are ideal
The Espada variety and others from the Zambezi Valley are extraordinary
A ripe, fresh mango cut and eaten is the Mozambican morning
No recipe is needed — the mango is the recipe
Squeezing lime over emphasizes the sweetness
Mozambique's mango season: October-January — the heat coincides with mango season
Mangoes are sold from street vendors, from trees in yards, at markets
The mango is as culturally central to Mozambique as the coconut is to Pacific islands
During mango season, mangoes feature at every meal, every snack, every moment
Mozambican mangoes are considered among the world's finest by chefs who have tasted them
breakfast.description: Mozambique's finest seasonal breakfast — a ripe fresh mango, eaten simply with a squeeze of lime. Mozambique produces exceptional mangoes (particularly the Espada variety from the Zambezi Valley). October-January mango season is a Mozambican cultural event: mangoes are everywhere, eaten at every opportunity. No preparation needed — the fruit is the recipe.

lunch.name: Piri Piri Prawns
ingredients: Piri piri sauce: bird's eye chili, garlic, lemon, oil, paprika
instructions: Blend piri piri sauce
Marinate prawns 30 min
Grill over high heat 3 min per side
Serve with lemon wedges and rice
lunch.description: Flame-grilled prawns in fiery piri piri sauce — Mozambique's most famous dish.

lunch.name: Xima com Caril (Cornmeal with Curry)
ingredients: Chicken curry: chicken, tomato, onion, coconut milk, curry powder
instructions: Make thick cornmeal porridge (xima)
Cook chicken curry with coconut milk
Serve xima with curry spooned over
lunch.description: Thick cornmeal porridge with coconut chicken curry.

lunch.name: Xima com Nhemba (Maize Porridge with Black-Eyed Peas)
ingredients: Xima (Mozambican maize porridge — same as nsima/sadza)
instructions: Xima is Mozambique's maize staple — identical to nsima (Malawi), ugali (Kenya), sadza (Zimbabwe)
Boil water, add maize flour gradually — stir vigorously
Cook until very thick and stiff — it holds its shape when scooped
Make nhemba (black-eyed pea relish): fry onion, garlic, tomato
Add boiled black-eyed peas — simmer 10 minutes
Season with salt and chili
Serve xima with nhemba poured over or alongside
Black-eyed peas were brought to Mozambique and spread to the Americas via the slave trade
The black-eyed pea is an African-origin legume that crossed the Atlantic with enslaved Africans
Xima com nhemba is the everyday Mozambican meal — affordable and nutritious
lunch.description: Mozambique's everyday meal — stiff maize porridge (xima) with a black-eyed pea relish in tomato and onion. Black-eyed peas are an African-origin legume that traveled to the Americas via the slave trade; eating them in Mozambique is eating at the origin. Xima is the southern African universal staple, called ugali, sadza, or nsima across the region.

lunch.name: Matapa (Cassava Leaf Stew)
ingredients: Young cassava leaves (pounded — same cyanide precaution as Madagascar)
Peanuts (ground — the Mozambican peanut addition distinguishes from other cassava leaf stews)
instructions: SAFETY: pound and boil cassava leaves as with all cassava preparations
Boil pounded cassava leaves — 30 minutes minimum — discard water, add fresh
The leaves become dark green and silky
Add coconut milk — the Mozambican addition that distinguishes from Malawian ravitoto
Add ground peanuts — another Mozambican signature layer
Add dried or fresh shrimp
Season with garlic and salt
Matapa is Mozambique's national signature dish
The cassava leaf + coconut milk + peanut combination is uniquely Mozambican
Neither the coconut milk nor the peanut appears in the Malawian version
The Portuguese gave the dish Portuguese-origin casserole technique; the indigenous components are Mozambican
lunch.description: Mozambique's national signature dish — pounded cassava leaves long-boiled, then combined with thick coconut milk, ground peanuts, and shrimp. The triple combination of cassava leaves + coconut milk + peanuts is uniquely Mozambican (neighboring Malawi uses no coconut milk or peanuts in its cassava leaf stew). Matapa is the most distinctive Mozambican dish.

dinner.name: Camarão Grelhado (Grilled Shrimp)
instructions: Butterfly prawns
Grill with garlic butter and piri piri
Squeeze lemon
Serve with fries and salad
dinner.description: Butterflied grilled prawns in garlic butter.

dinner.name: Frango à Zambeziana (Zambezi Chicken)
instructions: Marinate chicken in piri piri, lime, garlic
Brown chicken
Add coconut milk and onion
Simmer 30 min
dinner.description: Coconut-piri piri chicken from the Zambezi region.

dinner.name: Camarão Grelhado (Grilled Prawns)
ingredients: Tiger prawns (Mozambican — large, fresh, from the Indian Ocean)
instructions: Mozambique's Indian Ocean prawn fishery is world-renowned — Mozambican tiger prawns are exceptional
Butterfly the prawns — split down the back, press flat
Marinate in piri piri (chili-garlic-lemon oil) — 30 minutes minimum
Grill over charcoal or high heat — very fast (3-4 minutes)
Baste with garlic butter as they cook
The prawn should be just cooked — translucent gives way to opaque
Squeeze lemon generously
Mozambican grilled prawns are considered among the world's finest — the prawn quality is the reason
Served at every coastal restaurant, at Maputo's harbor, at beach restaurants in Tofo and Vilankulo
The combination of Indian Ocean prawn + piri piri chili is Mozambique's food identity
dinner.description: Mozambique's iconic Indian Ocean prawn — large tiger prawns butterflied, marinated in piri piri, grilled over charcoal 3-4 minutes, finished with garlic butter and lemon. Mozambican tiger prawns are internationally renowned. The piri piri + Indian Ocean prawn combination is Mozambique's food identity, exported to Portuguese restaurants worldwide.

dinner.name: Galinha à Zambeziana (Zambezi Chicken)
instructions: Galinha à zambeziana is Mozambique's regional chicken dish — from the Zambezi Valley
The combination: coconut milk + lime + chili is distinctly Mozambican coast
Marinate chicken in lime juice, garlic, piri piri, salt — 1 hour
Brown chicken in oil — the skin should be golden
Add coconut milk — simmer 25-30 minutes
The coconut milk and lime together create a bright, rich sauce
More piri piri at the end for heat
The lime keeps the coconut milk from being heavy
Galinha à zambeziana is the Mozambican chicken that Portuguese restaurants adapted
The Indian Ocean flavor profile: coconut, lime, chili is the coastal Mozambique signature
dinner.description: Mozambique's Zambezi Valley chicken — marinated in lime and piri piri, browned, then braised in coconut milk. The coconut milk + lime + piri piri combination is the coastal Mozambique flavor signature. The lime keeps the coconut from being heavy. Mozambique's most internationally recognized chicken dish, adapted in Portuguese-language restaurants worldwide.

dinner.name: Arroz com Feijão (Rice with Beans)
instructions: Mozambique's most common side dish — Portuguese rice culture meeting indigenous bean traditions
Fry onion, garlic in oil
Add tomato — cook down
Add boiled beans, season with salt, optional cumin
Cook rice separately — Mozambican rice is cooked slightly fluffy
Serve beans over rice — or serve side by side
Arroz com feijão is the Mozambican staple side dish for any protein
The Portuguese arroz (rice) + African feijão (bean) combination is Mozambican
Portugal gave rice cultivation; Africa gave beans — the hybridity is the Mozambican food identity
The cumin addition shows Arabic-Indian Ocean trade route influence
dinner.description: Mozambique's everyday side — fluffy white rice alongside kidney beans in a tomato-onion sauce. The Portuguese arroz (rice cultivation) meets African feijão (bean traditions): the colonial hybrid that has become completely Mozambican. Cumin sometimes added — the Arabic-Indian Ocean trade route spice reaching inland Mozambique.

snacks.name: Chamuças (Samosas)
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, onion, chili, curry
instructions: Cook spiced meat filling
Fill dough triangles
Fry until golden

snacks.name: Pão com Amendoim (Peanut Bread Spread)
ingredients: Homemade peanut paste (ground roasted peanuts with salt and a little oil)
instructions: Roast peanuts in a dry pan until fragrant and slightly darkened
Grind in a mortar or food processor with salt and a small amount of oil
The peanut paste should be thick and slightly coarse — not as smooth as commercial peanut butter
Spread generously on soft mapão
Mozambique is a significant peanut producer
The homemade peanut paste is a staple snack and breakfast spread
The peanut-bread combination is eaten across all Mozambican communities
The homemade paste has a rougher, more intensely flavored quality than commercial
Ground peanut paste appears in matapa, in sauces, in snacks — it's Mozambique's most versatile ingredient
snacks.description: Mozambique's peanut bread — freshly ground roasted peanuts with salt spread thickly on soft mapão rolls. Mozambique is a significant peanut producer; homemade peanut paste is rougher and more intensely flavored than commercial peanut butter. Peanuts appear throughout Mozambican cooking (matapa, sauces, snacks) — this is peanuts in their most immediate, direct form.

snacks.name: Bolinhos de Amendoim (Peanut Cookies)
instructions: Mix ground peanuts with sugar and egg — the egg binds the peanut and sugar
Optional: add small amount of flour for easier handling
Shape into small balls or flatten into discs
Bake at 175°C until just set — 12-15 minutes
The peanut-sugar combination caramelizes slightly
Cool completely before eating — they firm as they cool
Bolinhos de amendoim are Mozambique's peanut cookie — the Portuguese 'bolinho' (small cake) with African peanut
The Portuguese baking tradition adapted to local peanut abundance
Found at markets, bakeries, and home bakers throughout Mozambique
The crispy peanut cookie is satisfying and simple
snacks.description: Mozambique's peanut cookie — ground roasted peanuts with sugar and egg, shaped and baked until the edges caramelize. The Portuguese bolinho (small cake) technique adapted to Mozambique's peanut abundance. Found at markets and home bakers. The crispy, caramelized peanut edges and the simple sweetness are the pleasure.

snacks.name: Frango Frito (Fried Chicken Mozambican Style)
ingredients: Lemon juice, garlic, piri piri, salt (marinade)
instructions: Marinate chicken in lemon, garlic, piri piri, salt — minimum 1 hour (overnight ideal)
The acid marinade tenderizes and adds the citrus-chili flavor
Dredge in flour lightly — just enough for a thin coating
Fry in hot oil until golden and cooked through
The piri piri in the marinade adds heat throughout the meat — not just on the surface
The lemon gives brightness against the fried fat
Mozambican fried chicken is distinguished by the piri piri marinade — Portuguese-African
Served with rice and xima (maize porridge)
The piri piri chicken concept traveled from Mozambique to Portugal via the Portuguese colonial return — Nando's (the piri piri chain) is based on this Mozambican culinary tradition
snacks.description: Mozambique's piri piri fried chicken — marinated overnight in lemon, garlic, and piri piri chili, lightly floured and fried. The piri piri marinade permeates the meat (not just the surface). This is the Mozambican culinary tradition that Nando's (the global piri piri chain) is based on — the recipe traveled from Mozambique to Portugal with returning colonists and then globally.

desserts.name: Bolo Polana (Cashew Nut Cake)
instructions: Beat eggs with sugar
Add ground cashews and mashed potato
Add butter and vanilla
Bake at 175°C 40 min
desserts.description: Cashew nut cake with mashed potato — Mozambique's signature dessert.

desserts.name: Coco Gelado (Coconut Ice Lolly)
instructions: Mix coconut milk with sugar and lime juice
Adjust sweetness and acidity — should be pleasantly sweet and slightly tart
Optional: vanilla for fragrance
Pour into popsicle molds or small cups
Freeze until solid — at least 4 hours
Coco gelado is Mozambique's ice treat — made at home and sold by street vendors
Mozambique's tropical heat makes ice treats essential
The coconut milk freeze creates a smooth, creamy ice unlike water-based popsicles
The fat in coconut milk slows melting — the ice stays firmer longer
Sold from cold boxes at beaches and markets in Mozambique's coastal cities
desserts.description: Mozambique's coconut ice lolly — thick coconut milk sweetened and acidified with lime, frozen until solid. The fat in coconut milk creates a creamier, slower-melting ice than water-based popsicles. Sold from cold boxes at Mozambican beaches and markets. The coconut-lime combination is the coastal Mozambique in frozen form.

desserts.name: Bolo Polvilhado (Cassava Cake)
ingredients: Cassava flour (tapioca flour — the dried, safe form)
instructions: Cassava flour (tapioca) is safe — it's the dried, processed form without cyanide
Mix cassava flour with eggs, sugar, butter, coconut milk, baking powder
The batter is slightly gelatinous from the tapioca — different from wheat flour
Pour into a buttered pan
Bake at 175°C until set — the cassava cake is denser than wheat cake
The texture is distinctive: slightly chewy, sticky, and dense — almost like a mochi cake
Cassava cake is Mozambique's (and much of Africa and Latin America's) primary non-wheat cake
The Portuguese bolo (cake) tradition adapted entirely to cassava flour
Polvilhado means 'dusted' — traditionally dusted with coconut
Very popular at Mozambican celebrations alongside wheat-flour cakes
desserts.description: Mozambique's cassava cake — tapioca flour (the safe, processed form) mixed with eggs, coconut milk, and butter, baked into a dense, slightly chewy cake with a mochi-like texture. Portuguese bolo tradition adapted entirely to Africa's primary starchy crop. The sticky, dense cassava texture is completely unlike wheat cake — an acquired pleasure.

drinks.name: 2M Beer
instructions: Serve ice cold
The national beer
drinks.description: Mozambique's favorite beer — always served freezing cold.

drinks.name: Tipo Tinto (Cashew Wine)
instructions: Press cashew apples for juice
Let ferment 3-5 days
Strain and serve
drinks.description: Wine fermented from cashew apple juice.

drinks.name: Sura (Palm Wine)
ingredients: Fresh palm wine (tapped from various palm species — Roystonea, Borassus, or others)
instructions: Sura is Mozambique's traditional palm wine — fresh tapped sap from palm trees
Similar to Maldivian kanaa or Mauritanian toddy
Fresh: mildly sweet, slightly fizzy, non-alcoholic
After 12-24 hours: mildly alcoholic, more sour
After several days: strongly alcoholic, very sour
The timing of drinking determines the experience
Mozambique's coastal and inland palm trees provide sura in palm-growing regions
The palm wine tradition is shared across sub-Saharan Africa (Kenya, Nigeria, Congo, Mozambique)
Sura is drunk fresh in the morning for sweetness, or fermented for celebration
The palm wine economy: tappers climb palms daily, collect sap, sell or drink it
The fresh fizzy sweetness of morning palm sap is one of tropical Africa's most pleasant flavors
drinks.description: Mozambique's fresh palm wine — sap tapped daily from palm trees, drunk fresh (sweet, slightly fizzy, non-alcoholic) or allowed to ferment for alcohol. The timing determines everything: morning fresh sap is pure sweetness; evening sap is mildly alcoholic and sour; several-days-old sap is strongly alcoholic. The pan-African palm wine tradition from coastal Mozambique to inland regions.
